title: Randomized simulation of a nondeterministic program
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with initial label $l_0$, oracle, and decider machine $D$ with initial states $q_0$ and space bound $B$. Fix an input $x$, register values $v$, output prefix $out$, and natural numbers $W,N$. Suppose every sequence of $N$ choice bits makes the program halt, and each configuration before halting satisfies the guard: its applicable instruction preconditions hold, every decider call has distinct argument registers and a clean run using at most $B$ work-head cells, and each register value $z$ satisfies $|	ext{the binary length of }z+1|\le W$. Then there is a number $T$ such that the compiled nondeterministic Turing machine halts on every choice sequence of length $T$, and for each $b\in\{0,1\}$ the fraction of length-$T$ choice sequences producing output $out$ followed by $b$ equals the fraction of length-$N$ sequences on which the register program's final answer is $b$.
hypotheses_covered: Nondeterministic register program and initial label
Oracle, decider machine, initial-state map, and bounds B and W
Fixed input x, register values v, output prefix out, and choice length N
Every active proper-prefix configuration satisfies NGuard, including instruction preconditions, clean bounded-space decider calls, and register binary-length bounds
